title: Finite affine source charts over an affine target neighbourhood
statement: Let $X,Y,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $q:X\to Y$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and surjective on points, and let $h:Y\to S$ satisfy that $h\circ q$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every $y\in Y$ there exist affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with $h(y)\in V$, $y\in W$, and $W\subseteq h^{-1}(V)$, an integer $n\geq0$, and affine opens $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i\subseteq X$, $1\leq i\leq n$, contained in $q^{-1}(W)$, such that $W=\bigcup_{i=1}^n q(U_i)$. The induced coordinate maps form towers $R\to A\to B_i$; each $A\to B_i$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and each composite $R\to B_i$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. No quasi-compactness or separation assumption is made on $q$, $h$, or $X,Y,S$.

source.place: Tag 02KL (lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence), locally-of-finite-type alternative; Proof, first sentence and the sentences selecting finitely many affine opens whose images cover the affine target; old item steps 1-3, including all three affine-pair coordinate criteria.

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$. By the affine-open basis, choose an affine open $V\subseteq S$ containing $h(y)$, then an affine open $W\subseteq Y$ with $y\in W\subseteq h^{-1}(V)$; the latter inverse image is open by continuity of the scheme morphism. Put $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$ and $A=\mathcal O_Y(W)$.

source.place: Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens; applied twice as in the local reduction of Tag 02KL

proof.text: Let $\mathcal U$ be the set of affine opens $U\subseteq X$ contained in $q^{-1}(W)$. The affine-open basis covers $q^{-1}(W)$ by these $U$. Since $q$ is surjective, every $w\in W$ has a preimage $x$, and some $U\in\mathcal U$ contains $x$; hence $W=\bigcup_{U\in\mathcal U}q(U)$. Flatness and local finite presentation make $q$ open, so each $q(U)$ is open in $Y$ and contained in $W$. The affine scheme $W$ is quasi-compact; by the finite-subcover definition choose finitely many $U_1,\ldots,U_n\in\mathcal U$ with $W=\bigcup_{i=1}^nq(U_i)$. This selects images covering $W$ and does not assert that the selected opens cover $q^{-1}(W)$.

source.place: Tag 02KL, lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence, proof: openness and finite affine selection; inputs Tags 01IT, 01UA and 00E8

proof.text: Put $B_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$. The containments $q(U_i)\subseteq W$ and $h(W)\subseteq V$ give coordinate maps $R\to A\to B_i$. Functoriality of the structure-sheaf maps in the composite scheme morphism identifies their composite with the coordinate map for $h\circ q$ on $(U_i,V)$. These are the canonical affine presentations $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, up to their canonical isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 02KL, proof, final affine translation; functorial induced coordinate maps

proof.text: Apply the flat affine-pair criterion to $q$ and $(U_i,W)$ to obtain that $A\to B_i$ is flat. Apply the locally-finite-presentation affine-pair criterion to the same $q,U_i,W$ to obtain finite presentation of $A\to B_i$. Finally $(h\circ q)(U_i)\subseteq V$, so the locally-finite-type affine-pair criterion for $h\circ q$ and $(U_i,V)$ shows that $R\to B_i$ is of finite type. All criteria apply to arbitrary affine pairs; they impose no quasi-compactness or separation hypotheses on the original morphisms or schemes. The charts and coordinate maps satisfy every required clause.
